cells.tense: Meaning is moving through you now, and the practice is where it lands.
cells.act: tell the truth with care for when and how
cells.ask: Pick a person and a true thing you've been circling. Say it plainly once, at a moment that can hold it. Don't wait to feel ready first.
cells.core:
You can feel a thing and hand it on in the same motion. What you keep at alone, in the repetitions nobody watches, is where that motion gets tested — you find out in private whether the meaning is real enough to carry, and it is. Then something you say out loud lands further than you threw it, and you can see it land. That is the light here: it doesn't just burn, it arrives. Inside, you're still making this rather than living in something finished, and the practice is what holds it while it isn't.

One dial is worth touching. When you say the true thing, match it to the listener — the person, the day, the size they can take. Doing that on purpose, rather than from the first full feeling, is the whole of it. Say it once, plainly, and stop there for now.
cells.sheetLine: You mean it, you keep at it, and it lands further than you threw it.
cells.verb: charging toward what connects, and passing it on
cells.place: in the small steady light of a practice you keep by attention

cells.tense: You will have already pictured it finished, and the beginning will feel too slow to bother with.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Take a piece of the practice all the way through, then stop for the day. Leave the rest unfinished on purpose.
cells.core:
The whole thing is already in your head — the finished form, the person it turns, the day it finally runs without you — and the glow of it outruns what your hands can do this evening. So the practice gets planned more than done, or done at the pitch the picture wants, which is a pitch the work doesn't have yet. That pull is real and it's yours. It has simply been arriving before the thing it wants.

A change that lasts gets pressed in an inch at a time by steady work, and the pacing isn't yours to argue with. So take one real inch. One piece of the session, done all the way, and stop there today — not because small is virtuous, but because being there while it's small is what gets you there when it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: The finished picture keeps arriving before the work does.
cells.verb: charging toward what connects, and passing it on
cells.place: in the small steady light of a practice you keep by attention

cells.tense: You were carried toward people by feeling once, and you have stayed at the edge of your practice since.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Work out by reasoning what you'd do if the meaning were certain, then do that one thing today. Skip the debate with yourself.
cells.core:
The practice is still there — hands moving, sessions kept, the light maintained out of habit — but nothing you make in it is going anywhere. Meaning stopped being passed because no one is at the door to hand it to. You keep the altar lit without an idea of who it's for. The practice is waiting, and you are standing just past the place where it once carried you into a room.

One thing, thought through fast and clean, gives a starving seat something to run on. So settle a single question by reasoning rather than by how you feel: name plainly what you'd do if the meaning were certain, and do it today. Not the feeling — the course. Making the meaning concrete is what puts your hands back on it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the practice lit and nothing in it is going anywhere.
cells.verb: charging toward what connects, and passing it on
cells.place: in the small steady light of a practice you keep by attention

cells.tense: Others are taking a shape from how you practise, and you have never once said that you meant it.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Somebody asks what you're practising for — answer with one plain true sentence about the thing itself, sized to them. Not a speech.
cells.core:
You give people something solid. The way you keep at the thing, the same way again and again, becomes a floor for whoever is watching, and they take it without being told to — a rhythm to stand on. The meaning already gets to them. What's missing is its name. You say you're just keeping your hand in. That's the same mistrust, in words, of the thing doing its work through you.

So say one honest sentence about it. When the question comes, answer plainly at the size they can hear, once, and don't take it back. Not where it's going — just the true thing out loud. You've been calling your practice a habit; the ones who watch have noticed what it is, and have been waiting for you to know it too.
cells.sheetLine: What others take from your practice is what you haven't said out loud.
cells.verb: charging toward what connects, and passing it on
cells.place: in the small steady light of a practice you keep by attention

attempts.check: The record names the seat's content and the medicine's acts, but nothing about this person's week — so the core must stay on what the capacity is and what it is doing in a recognizable moment, never on what happened to them. A reader could fairly say 'I've never tried to teach anyone; this isn't my life' — the signature's teaching may be nothing more than meaning passed hand to hand in a practice, so the cells keep it at that size and don't lean on a classroom. The asks each work even if the read is wrong, because each is a small concrete move a person can do or decline without owing anything. The sentence that serves me more than them is any claim that this balance is 'finally' arrived at or a reward for years of work; that gets cut.
